api_products.description: List of API products associated with the developer app.
api_products.rationale: This is a list of API products the developer app can access. Which products are appropriate depends entirely on the app's purpose and the team's API architecture. A generic platform policy cannot determine which products every team should associate with their apps without team-specific knowledge.

app_family.rationale: This is an organisational grouping label for developer apps. It is purely metadata with no effect on security posture, authentication, or how the app accesses APIs.

callback_url.description:
Callback URL used by OAuth 2.0 authorization servers to communicate
authorization codes back to developer apps.
callback_url.rationale: This is the OAuth 2.0 redirect URI used by authorization servers to communicate authorization codes back to the app. While security-relevant in OAuth flows (open redirectors can lead to authorization code theft), the specific URL is inherently team-specific. A Rego policy using whitelist or blacklist helpers can only check exact values, not patterns such as requiring an HTTPS prefix. A meaningful constraint would require team-specific URLs, which is not a generic platform policy.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform can destroy the developer app. The default value of DELETE allows unrestricted destructive operations. Deleting a developer app immediately revokes its consumer key, breaking any clients using that key. A generic platform policy can require this to be set to PREVENT, blocking accidental or unauthorized deletion of developer apps and their consumer credentials at the platform level without requiring team-specific values.

developer_email.description:
Email address of the developer.
This value is used to uniquely identify the developer in Apigee hybrid.
Note that the email address has to be in lowercase only.
developer_email.rationale: This is the email address identifying the developer who owns the app. The value is inherently team-specific. A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific developer email addresses.

key_expires_in.rationale: This controls the expiration time in milliseconds for the consumer key (API key) generated for the developer app. The default value of -1 means the key never expires, and this setting is immutable after creation. Per GCP documentation, non-expiring API keys are a security risk because if compromised, they remain valid indefinitely with no forced rotation. A generic platform policy can blacklist the value -1 to enforce that all consumer keys have a finite expiration, promoting regular key rotation and limiting the impact of compromised credentials. No team-specific values are needed.

name.rationale: This is the name of the developer app. It is a naming identifier with no effect on security posture, authentication, or API access controls.

org_id.description:
The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee instance,
in the format 'organizations/{{org_name}}'.
org_id.rationale: This is a reference to the parent Apigee Organization. The value is inherently team- or project-specific. A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific organization identifiers. The security of the organization itself is governed by the google_apigee_organization resource.

scopes.description:
Scopes to apply to the developer app.
The specified scopes must already exist for the API product that
you associate with the developer app.
scopes.rationale: These are the OAuth scopes the developer app can request. Which scopes are appropriate depends entirely on the app's purpose and the API products it consumes. A generic platform policy cannot determine which scopes every team should use without team-specific knowledge.

status.description: Status of the credential. Valid values include approved or revoked.
status.rationale: This controls the credential status of the developer app (approved or revoked). The typical provisioning workflow requires apps to be approved to function. Forcing all apps to start revoked would break normal workflows. The choice between approved and revoked is an operational decision managed per-app by the team.

attributes.description: Developer attributes (name/value pairs). The custom attribute limit is 18.

attributes.name.rationale: This is a custom attribute key for team-specific metadata on the developer app. Custom attributes are informational name/value pairs with no effect on authentication, authorization, or security posture.

attributes.value.rationale: This is a custom attribute value for team-specific metadata on the developer app. Custom attributes are informational name/value pairs with no effect on authentication, authorization, or security posture.
